reports.title: WARNER MUSIC GROUP CORP. REPORTS RESULTS FOR FISCAL FOURTH QUARTER AND FULL YEAR ENDED SEPTEMBER 30, 2026

desk.headline: Record quarter: revenue up 7% to $2.0bn and adjusted EPS $0.55, both beat; fiscal 2027 outlook for further growth and margin gains
results: Revenue rose 7% to a record $2.0bn; digital revenue grew 13% and Recorded Music subscription streaming 15%.
Adjusted OIBDA rose 18% to $477m and the margin widened to 23.8%, helped by cost savings; GAAP net income climbed to $179m.
Artist services fell 21% against a strong prior-year quarter boosted by Oasis merchandise; physical sales rose 28%.
Full year: revenue up 11% to $7.4bn, adjusted EPS $2.03 (from $1.67) and free cash flow up 42% to $766m.
Quarterly operating cash flow fell 32% to $158m on timing of restructuring payments and advances to streaming services; net debt ended at $4.1bn.

guidance.summary: The press release gives no figures. On the call, as reported, management pointed to high-single-digit revenue growth in fiscal 2027, double-digit adjusted OIBDA and EPS growth and about 1 point of margin gain.

items.metric: Adjusted OIBDA and adjusted EPS growth

points: AI licensing is set to become a material revenue source in fiscal 2027, led by the licensed Suno music model.
Contract renewals with big streaming services, including Spotify, are under negotiation; price rises keep helping into Q1 before being lapped.
Margin gains came from restructuring and cost control; about $100m of restructuring cash went out in the year.
Management flagged weak spots: lower Q4 cash flow, no share gains in Asia-Pacific and softer artist services and some publishing lines.
The sale of EMP removes about $180m of revenue from the comparison base.
call.source: Call coverage: TipRanks, 20 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: Whether AI licensing revenue actually shows up in fiscal 2027 numbers.
